sovereign_country.strategic_role: 极速离岸证券与外汇交易商持牌（VFSC）、轻资产免税出海

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Light Value-Added Postponement Packaging and Custom Kitting

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Vanuatu (Unitary National Jurisdiction; Registered Agent Regime administered in Port Vila)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (English Common Law heritage with French Civil Law influence; bijural system). International Company regime governed exclusively by the International Companies Act [Cap 222], administered by the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: PACER Plus (Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus, in force 2020)
No comprehensive double tax agreement network currently in force

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act [Cap 222] (as amended 2011 and 2014); Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act No. 13 of 2021 (AML/CFT Act 2021) and its Regulations; VFSC Registered Agent Licensing Rules; VFIU Guidance Notes; UN and domestic terrorist designation lists.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport (every director, shareholder, UBO, and authorised signatory)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority or notary public in country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Vanuatu is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention 1961; documents must be legalized via Vanuatu Ministry of Foreign Affairs or an accredited Vanuatu Honorary Consul)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Conduct / Police Clearance Certificate (all UBOs and directors)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police or criminal records bureau of country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization via Vanuatu diplomatic/consular post

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming account conduct and source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating qualifying bank (correspondent or licensed commercial bank)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each UBO (utility bill or bank statement, not older than 3 months)
Corporate extract and certificate of incorporation and good standing (when a UBO is a legal entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization via Vanuatu diplomatic/consular post

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, and authorized signatories against the VFIU consolidated list, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN list, EU and HM Treasury sanctions lists, and domestic Vanuatu terrorist designations. Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) mandatory for PEPs, families, and close associates; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification required at or above 10% ownership or control; negative news and adverse-media searches mandatory; ongoing transaction monitoring and periodic UBO re-verification at least annually or upon trigger events.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) Online e-Registry System (company name clearance module accessible via VFSC website, administered in conjunction with licensed registered agents)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Latin script (English and/or French alphabets). No mandatory Bislama or local-script transliteration. Names may include diacritical French characters, but must be represented in standard Latin characters for the register. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any name already registered or reserved in the VFSC register, and must be distinguishable by sight and sound.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon VFSC name rejection, the applicant (normally via the licensed registered agent) may file a written administrative appeal with the VFSC Registrar within 14 days of the rejection notice, accompanied by a revised name or legal argument on distinguishability. The Registrar must issue a determination within 21 days. If the administrative appeal is denied, the applicant may seek judicial review in the Supreme Court of Vanuatu within 30 days of the denial. Alternative names should be submitted simultaneously to avoid delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted and standard for non-resident International Companies. The registered agent's licensed office in Port Vila serves as the statutory registered office; no physical presence, employees, or leased premises in Vanuatu are required for a non-resident low-risk IC conducting offshore fulfillment kitting and assembly paper-company operations. The commercial 3PL operations location is not required to be in Vanuatu.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated under 5% probability per annum for a non-resident, low-risk, tax-exempt IC). Unannounced inspections are generally triggered by suspicious activity reports, non-filing of annual returns, agent non-compliance, or adverse intelligence; a dormant or custodian IC with annual return compliance faces minimal inspection risk.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: VFSC company name reservation and clearance search fee
VFSC incorporation and first-year registration fee (International Company, non-resident)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: International Companies Act [Cap 222] fee schedule (approximate USD equivalent of VT 25,000 statutory tariff)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Licensed registered agent and registered office service (first year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate for non-resident IC maintenance, agent acceptance, and statutory record keeping

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO file compilation, AML/CFT CDD, and PEP/OFAC/UN sanctions screening
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered agent AML compliance officer / external compliance consultant
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for standard-risk non-resident IC CDD; AML/CFT Act 2021 compliance obligations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and consular legalization bundle (passport, police clearance, bank reference, proof of address, corporate extract)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public in origin country + Vanuatu Ministry of Foreign Affairs / Honorary Consul
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular fee schedules and prevailing notarial market rates; Vanuatu is non-Apostille jurisdiction

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: International courier and document expedition fees
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market courier tariff for certified original hard copies

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act [Cap. 222] (No. 32 of 1992, as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2014), read with the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission Act No. 22 of 2019 and the Companies Act No. 25 of 2018
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), Reserve Bank Building, Port Vila, Vanuatu
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 Registration Statement accompanied by the Memorandum and Articles of Association (Constitutional Documents), filed electronically by the licensed registered agent
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The International Companies Act [Cap. 222] imposes no minimum authorized or paid-up capital and no escrow account is required; at least one (1) share of no par value must be allotted to the subscriber.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscriber's subscription of one (1) ordinary share of no par value, fully paid and credited as paid, is hereby approved and the subscriber entered in the register of members. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office of the Company is fixed at [Registered Agent Address], Port Vila, Vanuatu, and [Registered Agent Name] is appointed as registered agent under the International Companies Act [Cap. 222]. RESOLVED FURTHER that [Director Name(s)] are appointed first directors, [Officer Name] is appointed Company Secretary, the common seal is adopted, and the banking mandate established. RESOLVED FURTHER that the directors are authorized to open the Company's exempt non-resident bank account, pay all incorporation fees, and take all actions necessary to perfect the Company's incorporation and tax-exempt status.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance and Registered Agent Retainer
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) Companies Registry, through an approved VFSC-licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit two proposed company names (English/French) for prior approval via the registered agent; ensure the name does not contain restricted expressions such as 'Bank', 'Trust', 'Assurance', 'Insurance' or 'Reinsurance' without a separate statutory license; after clearance, execute the registered agent engagement letter and retain the agent for the statutory registered office and registered agent duties.
required_dossiers: Proposed name search request form
Registered agent engagement letter
Certified copy of beneficial owner passport or national ID
Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as undesirable, misleading, or prohibited, file a fresh name request with two alternative names; appeal to the VFSC Registrar under section 5 of the International Companies Act within 14 days with supporting justifications.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Constitutional Documents (Memorandum and Articles of Association)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered agent (drafting) and notary public / subscriber (execution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association based on the standard International Company form; include the permitted objects of warehousing, logistics, kitting, and value-added packaging; a statement of tax-exempt offshore status; no-par-value share class provisions; and director powers. The sole subscriber executes the M&A and consents to act; notarization is not mandatory but attested copies of subscriber KYC documents must be attached.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (English draft)
Subscriber consent and signature page
KYC file (passport, proof of address, bank or agent references)
Certificate of incorporation and good standing certificate of corporate subscriber, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Vary the M&A by a written amendment signed by the subscriber before filing; any clerical error in the signed copy is cured by a supplementary amendment filed through the registered agent with the VFSC.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission to VFSC and Payment of Government Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent lodges the incorporation package electronically on the VFSC portal: Form 1 Registration Statement, executed M&A, consents of first directors and secretary, and payment of the USD 300 government fee (plus optional USD 100 express fee). The agent confirms the requested date of incorporation; funds are remitted by wire from a non-resident corporate or personal account.
required_dossiers: Form 1 Registration Statement
Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consent to act as director
Consent to act as company secretary
VFSC government fee payment receipt
Registered agent certification letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: VFSC issues a query or rejection notice; the registered agent has 14 days to respond with corrective documents; on expiry without a cure, the application is treated as withdrawn and prepaid fees may be applied to a resubmission or refunded at the VFSC's discretion.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Inception of Legal Personality
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar enters the Company into the International Companies Register and issues the Certificate of Incorporation stating the IC number and date of incorporation; the Company comes into existence on that date. The agent collects the Certificate and certified copies and prepares the initial statutory registers of members, directors, and secretary at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (issued by VFSC)
Endorsed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Initial register of members, directors, and secretary
Receipt of statutory registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectification of clerical errors in the certificate or register is effected by application to the Registrar under section 13 of the International Companies Act; a re-issued certificate retains the original incorporation date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution, Bank Account Opening, and Ancillary Physical Licenses
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors through the registered agent; Vanuatu Customs and Inland Revenue (Business License); Department of Labour; municipal fire and building authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or pass a written resolution: allot the initial share to the subscriber, fix the registered office, appoint officers, adopt the common seal and banking mandate, and open the non-resident exempt bank account. If a physical warehouse is to operate in Vanuatu, lodge the Business License application under the Business License Act [Cap. 248], the environmental registration with DEPC, the fire safety certificate application, and biosecurity clearance for pallets and kitting materials.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Memorandum and Articles of Association
First Board Resolution (share allotment, registered office, officers, bank mandate)
Director and secretary identity documents
Business License application and warehouse floor plan
DEPC environmental registration form
Fire safety certificate application and biosecurity import declaration for packaging materials
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Business License is refused on zoning grounds, apply to the municipal planning committee for a permissible-use determination or relocate the warehouse to an approved industrial zone; board resolutions may be re-passed and re-filed with the registered agent.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Vanuatu Investment Promotion Authority (VIPA) one-stop shop jointly with the Business License Branch, Vanuatu Customs and Inland Revenue, Ministry of Finance and Economic Management
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business License (Warehouse and Storage – Fulfillment Kitting and Value-Added Packaging) issued under the Business License Act [Cap. 248]

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environmental Protection and Conservation (DEPC), Ministry of Climate Change Adaptation, Meteorology, Geo-Hazards, Energy, Environment and National Disaster Management
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – Environmental Impact Assessment Review and Registration under section 11 of the Environmental Protection and Conservation Act [Cap. 283]; full EIA Report waived for non-hazardous warehousing and kitting operations below 1,000 square meters gross floor area; DEPC issues a registration certificate with operational conditions.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero unauthorized liquid discharge to public drains or stormwater systems; stormwater discharge within pH 6.0–9.0 and total suspended solids below 50 mg/L; no open burning of packaging waste; offcuts and obsolete packaging must be segregated, recycled, or exported in accordance with the Basel and Waigani Convention transboundary movement procedures; only water-based cold adhesives permitted, keeping workplace VOC concentrations below 50 ppm TWA; wooden pallets and kitting materials must meet Vanuatu Department of Biosecurity phytosanitary requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Vanuatu Police Force Fire and Rescue Services; Building Permit and structural load clearance from the Department of Public Works and Port Vila City Council; Occupational Health and Safety registration with the Department of Labour under the Employment Act No. 22 of 2018, including annual workplace inspection, documented fire evacuation drills, emergency lighting, fire extinguisher maintenance log, and adequate first-aid provision based on employee headcount.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Vanuatu Customs and Inland Revenue Department, Ministry of Finance and Economic Management; national VAT and tax administration portal: https://vat.gov.vu and ASYCUDA World customs clearance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing a fulfilment/kitting operation in Vanuatu must apply for a Taxpayer Identification Number and VAT Registration with the Vanuatu Customs and Inland Revenue Department via the prescribed form before commencing taxable activity or immediately upon exceeding the VAT registration threshold. The application must include the certificate of incorporation, the International Company registered agent details, constitutional and corporate ownership documents, local place of business evidence, projected taxable turnover and export volume descriptions. The Department verifies the application and issues a Taxpayer Identification Number and VAT Registration Certificate. Non-resident international companies with no physical presence or taxable activity in Vanuatu are not required to obtain a domestic TIN for offshore operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone; the Vanuatu International Company is an offshore non-resident entity under the International Companies Act and is outside the normal Vanuatu income tax net. No income tax, corporation tax, capital gains tax, dividend tax or withholding tax is imposed on non-resident offshore income; however, a physical kitting and fulfilment centre in Vanuatu that makes taxable supplies is subject to VAT compliance and must register once the statutory turnover threshold is exceeded.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Vanuatu does not provide a check-the-box entity classification election or hybrid-mismatch elections. The International Company is statutorily classified as a non-resident offshore entity. For VAT, a person whose taxable turnover is below the statutory threshold may elect voluntary registration, and a registered person may apply for deregistration when no longer carrying on taxable activity. No group VAT registration, cash accounting election or simplified annual VAT election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax under the Value Added Tax Act No. 11 of 2014, administered locally as Goods and Services Tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Vatu (VT) 5,000,000 of taxable supplies in any consecutive 12-month period; persons making exclusively zero-rated export supplies are taxable persons and are required to register when the threshold is met. A foreign International Company with a Vanuatu fulfilment centre is considered to have a taxable activity and must monitor taxable turnover, including zero-rated export supplies, for registration purposes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Vanuatu does not currently mandate a real-time e-invoicing fiscal clearance system, SAF-T reporting or digital stamping. Registered persons must issue VAT invoices containing prescribed particulars, including the supplier's name, Taxpayer Identification Number, VAT Registration Number, recipient details, description of goods or services, VAT rate and VAT amount. Customs export declarations are lodged electronically through ASYCUDA World and must be aligned with the supporting export evidence retained for VAT zero-rating and refund purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A VaRit registration supplies of goods and ancillary kitting, packaging and assembly services qualify for the zero per cent VAT rate when the goods are physically exported from Vanuatu by the supplier or on the supplier's behalf, are exported within the statutory removal window commonly applied in Vanuatu of 28 days from the time of supply, and are supported by evidence of export to a destination outside Vanuatu. The zero-rating treatment also applies to international transport-related supplies and to services supplied to non-resident persons in respect of goods located outside Vanuatu. A registered fulfilment operator must show that the goods left Vanuatu and that the services performed were integral to the export supply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration approved by Vanuatu Customs through ASYCUDA World
Bill of Lading or signed Air Waybill showing the port of discharge or destination outside Vanuatu
Commercial invoice and underlying sale or fulfilment services contract identifying the foreign buyer and the ownership of the exported goods
Packing list and itemised bill of materials for kitting, packaging and assembly services
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT/payment advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds from the foreign purchaser
Shipping vessel or airline departure register, container seal records and other proof of physical movement out of Vanuatu
Zero-rated supply register and VAT invoice records linking each export declaration to the corresponding VAT return
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Vanuatu Customs and Inland Revenue Department may audit zero-rated export claims and input VAT refunds by reference to shipping and customs evidence, foreign-exchange receipts and movement records. If goods were not actually exported, were falsely documented, or export proceeds were not received and repatriated within the prescribed window, the zero rating is clawed back and VAT becomes payable at 12.5 per cent on the supply. Penalties include additional tax on the evaded or incorrectly claimed VAT, late payment interest, cancellation of input VAT credits, and criminal prosecution including fines and imprisonment for knowingly providing false export documents. Retrospective assessments may be issued for extended periods in cases of fraud or deliberate non-disclosure, and directors and registered agents may be held jointly liable.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of Vanuatu (RBV) — Port Vila; the sole monetary authority and prudential regulator of licensed commercial banks in Vanuatu, with supervisory responsibility over the national payment and settlement systems and the custody of official foreign-reserve assets, but without exchange-control administration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Vanuatu vatu (VUV) is freely convertible for both current-account and capital-account purposes. There are no exchange-control laws, no capital-account approval, and no restrictions on the establishment or operation of foreign-currency accounts. Profit remittance, dividend distribution, repayment of shareholder loans, and full repatriation of capital can be effected without central-bank authorization, subject only to standard banking due-diligence and financial-transaction reporting obligations under the Financial Transactions Reporting Act. Because Vanuatu operates a zero-tax, substance-sensitive offshore regime, the practical hurdle for a tax-exempt International Company is not convertibility but the ability to produce commercial and operational evidence that satisfies Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Know-Your-Customer (KYC) standards imposed by the international correspondent banks clearing vatu or foreign-currency wires.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Vanuatu imposes no statutory surrender obligation on export receipts, no mandatory conversion ratio into VUV, and no entry timeline for foreign-currency proceeds. Export proceeds may be retained in an offshore foreign-currency account, in a domestic VUV account, or in a multi-currency account at a licensed Vanuatu bank without penalty. The only compliance requirement is that the underlying export documentation — commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading/airway bills, customs export entries, and bank collection records — must be retained for a minimum of five years and produced to the bank or the Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit upon request as audit evidence of the legitimacy of the trade flows. No surrender certificate or central-bank form is required.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium with structural limitations. Cross-border digital electronic-money institutions (EMIs) such as Airwallex, Wise, Payoneer, and similar platforms can be onboarded as service providers to a Vanuatu International Company, offering multi-currency corporate accounts in AUD, USD, EUR, and GBP, as well as virtual-account and batch-payout capabilities. Their legal and operational viability is constrained by three factors: (1) they hold no Vanuatu banking or EMI licence and are accordingly not supervised by the RBV or the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC); (2) they cannot clear or hold VUV-denominated balances and must route all Vanuatu-related transactions through foreign correspondent banks; and (3) balances held with them are not covered by any Vanuatu deposit-protection arrangement. Therefore, EMIs are acceptable as a secondary liquidity engine for cross-border trade and ACH-based disbursements, but they cannot replace the relationship with a licensed Vanuatu commercial bank for local regulatory substance, VUV clearing, or capital escrow obligations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: As a general rule, a Vanuatu International Company intending to open a corporate bank account must ensure that every authorised signatory and every beneficial owner appears for a physical or equivalent identity verification. The preferred method is an in-person interview at the bank's Port Vila branch, or before a notary public engaged by the bank. Where remote opening is permitted, the bank will still require a live video-based identity check, with the Vanuatu registered agent physically present during the video session and countersigning all account-opening resolutions. For a non-resident director, a sworn declaration before a consular official of a Commonwealth jurisdiction may satisfy the physical interview requirement, but the majority of tier-1 institutions in Vanuatu retain discretion to demand a face-to-face meeting. The mandate is stricter for the capital escrow or wealth-management account classes, for which physical presence at the branch is virtually non-waivable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: International Company (IC) with tax-exempt status, non-resident directors, and no demonstrable economic substance in Vanuatu.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of Certificate of Incorporation and current Memorandum & Articles; registered agent's certificate of due diligence; physical address evidence, including a lease agreement, a recent utility invoice and office photographs; a payroll and staffing record showing that at least one director or compliance officer is physically employed in Vanuatu; a board resolution adopting an economic-substance policy; and a current annual return filed with the VFSC.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex beneficial ownership using trust, nominee shareholder, or multi-layer offshore structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trust instrument or nominee declaration; certificate of registration of the trust (where required); full name, residential address, passport copy and source-of-wealth statement of the settlor, trustee, protector and each beneficiary; a chart showing the 25%+ ownership through to the natural person; an official beneficial-ownership register prepared in the VFSC-prescribed form; and a banker's reference from an accepted institution covering the ultimate beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency ACH or Airwallex payment volumes inconsistent with a low-risk warehouse, kitting, and packaging business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three-way inventory reconciliation between purchase orders, warehouse movement logs and sales orders; customs entry/exit records for goods moving through the fulfilment centre; executed warehousing and kitting service contracts with at least three distinct e-commerce principals; monthly commercial invoices and packing lists matching the transaction value; a projected 12-month cash-flow model; and a written compliance narrative explaining the absence of unlicensed financial-activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from a group shareholder or connected party where the economic basis is not clearly evidenced.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed capital subscription agreement or intra-group shareholder loan agreement; board minutes authorising the receipt of funds; six months of bank statements from the remitting entity; a group structure chart with the ownership interests; a commercial assessment demonstrating the capital is required for purchase-order financing or inventory build-up; and a preliminary financial model showing debt-service capacity and source of repayment. This packet should be accompanied by an independent lawyer's opinion that the transaction has no money-laundering or tax-evasion indicators.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or shareholder-loan capital must be routed through a correspondent-capable commercial bank using a SWIFT MT103 message. The instruction should specify the beneficiary account at the Vanuatu bank and include in SWIFT Field 70 one of the following narrative tags: 'INCAP-IC' for equity injection, 'INLOAN-IC' for a shareholder loan, or 'SK-PURCHASE' for purchase-order funding. The remitting bank must transmit the sending institution's BIC, the borrower's Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) where available, and complete source-of-funds information. For settlement in USD, the preferred path is through an international intermediary in New York such as an ANZ New York correspondent or BNY Mellon; for AUD, through the Australian segment of ANZ; for EUR, through BRED Banque Populaire in France; and the receiving Vanuatu bank will convert to VUV at its spot rate if required. RBV authorisation is not required, but the Vanuatu receiving bank must tag the credit as a capital transaction and maintain a full audit trail, including the remittance instruction, confirmations, and a copy of the board resolution.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For supplier invoices and operational costs, the standard rail is a SWIFT MT103 message processed through the Vanuatu bank's foreign correspondent, with payment purposes coded 'PROP' (goods) or 'ADV-REFUND' (returns). Direct USD disbursements should instruct the beneficiary to settle via CHIPS or FedWire, while AUD disbursements clear through the Australian high-value settlement system via ANZ Australia. For high-value procurement invoices in excess of USD 50,000, an irrevocable documentary letter of credit (LC) is the recommended instrument, issued by the Vanuatu bank by SWIFT MT700 and payable by MT202 against a clean presentation of commercial documents; this mitigates counterparty risk and provides the necessary customs and compliance trail. VUV-denominated disbursements must be settled only through a licensed domestic clearing participant. Airwallex may be used as a virtual-account and batch-payment overlay for ACH and local card payouts in the United States, the European Union, Australia, and the United Kingdom, but every payment identifier must reconcile to a commercial invoice retained in the IC's ERP system.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forward (USD/VUV or AUD/VUV) executed with a licensed RBV-authorised commercial bank
FX Swap and rollover contracts on USD/VUV with spot and forward legs
Cross-currency swap between AUD and USD used to hedge balance-sheet and working-capital exposures
Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) on USD/VUV with an offshore credit institution under an ISDA Master Agreement and CSA
European-style vanilla currency options (call and put) on EUR/USD and AUD/USD offered through the bank's treasury trading desk

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Renewal of International Company Registration and Tax-Exempt Status Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), Registrar of International Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of incorporation each year; VFSC grants a 30-day grace period; filing and payment administered exclusively through the VFSC-licensed registered agent.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of 10% of the annual fee after the grace period; continued default (generally over 6 months) triggers notice and administrative strike-off from the International Companies Register under the International Companies Act [Cap 222], with loss of tax exemption and limitation of liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of Registered Office and Registered Agent Particulars (Agent-filed)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed within 30 days following each anniversary of incorporation; no separate filing holiday; must be coordinated with the annual renewal payment.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalty under Section 110 of the International Companies Act; repeated non-filing by the registered agent may result in agent deregistration and strike-off of the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Register Annual Confirmation and Change Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: VFSC Confidential Beneficial Ownership Register (submitted through registered agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation submitted with the anniversary renewal; any change in beneficial ownership must be reported within 30 days of the change; initial filing within 30 days of incorporation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monetary penalties and personal liability for directors and officers under the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2019 for false, incomplete, or late UBO information; willful non-compliance may result in criminal liability and strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit under the International Companies Act for a Vanuatu International Company of any size or turnover; audit is optional and only required if mandated by the company's articles, a parent company, a financier, or an overseas contracting counterparty.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No prescribed Vanuatu statutory framework for International Companies; IFRS or US GAAP voluntarily adopted is acceptable; the company must maintain accounting records sufficient to explain transactions and financial position under Section 97 of the International Companies Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The International Company must keep a register of beneficial owners at its registered office in Vanuatu. The registered agent must obtain, verify, and file UBO particulars with the VFSC at incorporation, within 30 days of any shareholding or control change, and submit an annual UBO confirmation with the renewal filing. The register is confidential and accessible to authorized Vanuatu authorities, not the public.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members and Share Transfers
Registered Office and Registered Agent Particulars

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 to 600 per year (VFSC-licensed registered agent fee inclusive of registered office and statutory register maintenance)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 to 6,000 (optional voluntary audit or compliance-ready financial statement compilation required by banks, customers, or parent group in the fulfillment/kitting sector)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% — Vanuatu levies no corporate income tax; International Companies are statutorily exempt from all income, profits, and capital taxes under the International Companies Act (Cap 222), evidenced by a Tax Exemption Certificate issued by the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Zero effective rate on worldwide profits for International Companies; no capital gains tax, no inheritance/estate tax, no payroll tax, and no branch profits tax on offshore-source business; VAT applies only to onshore consumption and qualifying domestic supplies, while export-oriented logistics and kitting services performed for non-resident counterparts are zero-rated or outside the VAT net for the ISIC 5210 3PL model.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: VFSC Annual Return (prescribed form under the International Companies Act, Cap 222, filed by the licensed Registered Agent through the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission online e-Registry). No corporate income tax return exists in the Vanuatu regime; this registry filing is the sole mandatory annual corporate filing for exempt International Companies.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within five (5) months after each anniversary of incorporation, aligned with the annual VFSC fee renewal cycle administered by the licensed Registered Agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered International Company name, VFSC company number, date of incorporation, and registered agent reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact Latin-script name as shown in the Certificate of Incorporation; no transliteration, trade-name, or alias substitution is permitted on the statutory return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical registered office address in Vanuatu and the licensed VFSC registered agent's identity and licence number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must appoint and maintain a fully licensed Vanuatu registered agent; the International Company cannot serve as its own registered office or agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full names, residential addresses, nationality, and passport/identity document numbers of all current directors and the company secretary.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A minimum of one director (natural person or corporate entity) is permitted; non-resident directors are eligible, but KYC proof of identity and proof of address must be held by the agent and produced to the VFSC on demand.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Issued Share Capital and Shareholders
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Number and class of issued shares, consideration received, and the full beneficial ownership chain up to ultimate natural persons.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident beneficial owners are allowed without minimum capital requirements; the complete ownership chain must be disclosed to the agent; bearer shares are prohibited under the Vanuatu AML/CFT framework.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration that no business has been conducted with Vanuatu resident persons and that no land or onshore assets are held or entitled to be held.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For ISIC 5210 fulfilment and kitting operations, confirm that all material counterparties are non-residents and that service contracts are governed by a foreign law; breach of this declaration voids the exemption and exposes the company to the general withholding tax regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Agent certification of ongoing compliance with Vanuatu's economic substance requirements for distribution and service centre business, including premises, employees, and core income-generating activity in Vanuatu.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Whenever kitting and assembly are subcontracted, the International Company must still demonstrate directed and managed activity in Vanuatu; the attestation must disclose any substance shortfall.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing accrues incremental late fees under the current VFSC fee schedule; arrears persisting beyond the grace period trigger a strike-off notice, administrative dissolution, and restoration costs. Knowingly false filings constitute criminal offences under the International Companies Act, punishable by statutory fine and/or imprisonment, with personal exposure for the signing directors.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Vanuatu VAT Return (form administered by the Vanuatu Inland Revenue, electronically lodged through the VIRD e-Services portal) — mandatory only where the International Company is VAT-registered for onshore procurement or where a taxable supply arises in Vanuatu; export kitting and logistics services to non-residents are generally zero-rated or outside the scope of VAT.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly (monthly filing option applies to higher-turnover VAT registrants)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within thirty (30) days after the end of each tax period under the Value Added Tax Act timetable prescribed by the Commissioner of Inland Revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: VAT registration number and the tax period being declared.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident International Company need not register where all significant supplies are made to non-residents; voluntary registration may be used to recover input VAT on qualifying Vanuatu costs only if the zero-rating rules are satisfied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable supplies at the standard rate, zero-rated supplies, and exempt supplies with supporting invoice references.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Kitting, labelling, consolidation, and postponement services physically performed in Vanuatu for overseas principals must be classified as zero-rated exports; retain shipping records, customs documentation, and contracts evidencing the export character of the services.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: VAT paid on local purchases (warehouse leases, utilities, subcontracted labour) that is creditable against output tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Input credit is allowed only where a valid VIRD tax invoice names the International Company; foreign costs without a Vanuatu VAT invoice are non-creditable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section D - Net VAT and Payment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of net VAT due or refundable, remitted by electronic transfer to the Vanuatu Inland Revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Excess input credits attributable to zero-rated exports are refundable, but refunds trigger heightened verification; keep all contracts, purchase orders, and bills of lading available for audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration signed by the taxpayer or authorised agent, together with the electronic lodgement timestamp.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The registered agent may sign under a power of attorney, but the beneficial owner remains jointly liable for any deliberate misdeclaration.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and late payment attract a statutory late-payment penalty plus a monthly accrual on the unpaid VAT under the Value Added Tax Act; negligent or fraudulent returns are subject to a 100% penalty and imprisonment, and VAT debts constitute a priority statutory claim against the company's onshore assets.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for International Companies making distributions to non-resident shareholders under the statutory exemption in the International Companies Act (Cap 222); the general statutory withholding rate of 15% under the Income Tax Act applies only where exempt status has been lost or breached.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Vanuatu applies its limited double taxation agreement network (Australia, Fiji, France, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, Solomon Islands, and the United Kingdom, supplemented by tax information exchange agreements). Because International Company dividends are statutorily exempt at source, no treaty claim is required for outbound IC distributions. Where a treaty reduction applies to interest or royalties paid by a non-exempt payer, the recipient must file a notice of treaty application with the Vanuatu Inland Revenue, submit a Certificate of Residence issued by the treaty counterparty tax authority, provide a beneficial ownership declaration, and notify the paying agent before payment; relief is granted only upon the Commissioner's determination.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding rates: 15% on gross royalties and 15% on gross interest paid by a Vanuatu payer to a non-resident. Exempt International Companies are not subject to withholding on outbound royalty or interest payments. Comprehensive treaty practice generally reduces royalties and interest to 10%, conditioned on beneficial ownership; interest derived by financial institutions may qualify for a further reduced rate under specific treaty articles.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No vatu-denominated Local File or Master File thresholds are codified because exempt International Companies pay no corporate income tax; the operative thresholds are those of the ultimate parent's tax jurisdiction, typically EUR 7,500,000 aggregate related-party turnover or USD 10,000,000 intercompany transactions in line with OECD Chapter V practice. For the ISIC 5210 kitting entity, a transfer pricing policy memorandum should nevertheless be retained documenting the arm's length remuneration for value-added logistics services in order to prevent recharacterisation by the onshore parent regulator.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (Comparable Uncontrolled Price) — applicable to standard kitting and packing services benchmarked against independent freight forwarders and contract packers
Resale Price Method — applicable where the International Company resells goods bundled with kitting services
Cost Plus Method — applicable to cost-intensive fulfilment, assembly, and postponement operations
TNMM (Transactional Net Margin Method) — the most frequently indicated method for 3PL logistics margin testing
Profit Split Method — applicable to integrated, shared-risk kitting platforms
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Vanuatu applies economic substance requirements to International Companies in fulfilment of its OECD BEPS and EU Code of Conduct commitments. Fulfilment, kitting, and related-party logistics activity constitutes a 'distribution and service centre business' relevant activity; the International Company must evidence physical premises, qualified local employees, local operating expenditure, and strategic decision-making in Vanuatu, and must file the annual economic substance notification with the VFSC. The standard-risk tier applicable to ISIC 5210 (no statutory licence, ACH/Airwallex payment rails, low AML risk) requires a proportionate but genuine substance footprint; a material shortfall triggers exchange of information with the foreign parent's tax authority under Vanuatu's competent authority agreements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion through Sham Offshore Arrangement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Vanuatu International Company as a paper invoicing entity for kitting services physically performed entirely in the foreign parent's jurisdiction, artificially shifting operating income from a high-tax country without any Vanuatu employees, premises, or management direction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Vanuatu: revocation of the tax exemption certificate, retroactive exposure to the 15% withholding tax regime, pecuniary penalties under the Income Tax Act, and referral to the VFSC for strike-off. Foreign jurisdiction: CFC and general anti-avoidance recharacterisation, denial of treaty benefits under the principal purpose test, accuracy-related penalties of up to 100% to 200% of the avoided tax, and interest accrual.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false exemption declarations face fines and imprisonment under Vanuatu law; in the foreign parent jurisdiction, shadow-director and participation-note theories may expose directors to civil restitution orders, director disqualification, and cross-border travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a letterbox International Company with a mailbox agent, no local bank account, no employees, and all kitting and assembly subcontracted to the ultimate parent's domestic warehouse while continuing to claim the Vanuatu exempt status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Vanuatu: rejection of the annual economic substance attestation, administrative penalties under Vanuatu's economic substance framework, removal from the register, and automatic exchange of information with the parent's jurisdiction under the multilateral competent authority agreement. Foreign jurisdiction: the foreign tax authority disregards the entity, applies PFIC or CFC taxation, and imposes late-payment and accuracy penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for false substance certifications and for restoration costs following strike-off; foreign courts may impose personal liability under economic substance and GAAR rules where the director controlled the substance-free structure, including freezing orders, travel restrictions, and contempt proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT Regulatory Breach and Illicit Fund Movements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving rapid in-and-out ACH or Airwallex payments sourced from unknown merchants, relying on unvetted payment intermediaries or crypto rails, failing to maintain the beneficial ownership register, or omitting suspicious transaction reports while acting as a payment conduit for fulfilment clients.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Vanuatu: penalties under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act, forfeiture of transaction proceeds, suspension of the registered agent's licence, and referral to the Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit for criminal prosecution; systemic breaches also trigger correspondent bank de-risking and reputational blacklisting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners face personal criminal liability, fines, and imprisonment for money laundering under Vanuatu law; regulators may impose personal travel bans pending investigation, and foreign counterparties can obtain asset freezes through mutual legal assistance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False Filings, Misrepresentation and Fraudulent Dissolution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Submitting the VFSC annual return with false declarations of no Vanuatu-resident business, concealing the true ultimate beneficial owner, using forged exemption certificates, or dissolving the International Company to evade outstanding VAT or contractual liabilities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Vanuatu: offences under the International Companies Act (Cap 222) and ancillary companies legislation; per-filing fines, compulsory deregistration, disqualification from conducting offshore activity in Vanuatu, and additional penalties under the fraud provisions of the Penal Code where documents were falsified.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal fines and imprisonment for false declarations and fraudulent trading; the court may pierce the corporate veil to hold directors personally liable for unpaid VAT, agent fees, and third-party contractual debts, and may bar them from operating any company registered in Vanuatu.
